title: host.v1: every message between the daemon and a plugin host ('csl-plugin-host/1')
description: One channel per loaded plugin; every load on a channel names the plugin the channel was opened for. This file holds every message on it. A plugin's whole world is the messages on its one channel to the daemon: the plugin imports nothing from Recursion and shares no object with the daemon. FRAMING: the length-prefixed frames of control_transport/framing.py, reused as they are: a 4-byte big-endian length, then that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON holding one object. FRAME SIZE: a load frame (daemon to host only) may be as large as the daemon's largest package needs: the daemon's largest manifest and largest package file (MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES and MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES of plugin_security/limits.py, the sizes daemon/plugins.py reads) as base64, plus the load's envelope with the longest plugin id; that limit is computed from those constants, never a second number. Every other frame, and every frame a host sends, is at most 1 MiB. A package that still does not fit one load frame is refused on the daemon's side with 'load_too_large' and is never sent; it is never a frame error. No load comes in parts in this release. Every byte string on the channel is standard base64 with padding, in a field whose name ends in '_b64'. THE MESSAGES (each in $defs): hello (each side, once, first); load (daemon to host: one plugin's id, its manifest bytes and its verified package files as bytes; load may arrive after hello at any time, even though the daemon sends it only at start in this release); call (either side: a call NAME taken from the one append-only list x-call-names, with its arguments; the daemon calls a plugin's function by name, and a plugin's host calls a broker handle by name); core (host to daemon: one csl-core/v0 request, its bytes unchanged; daemon to host: the core's answer, its bytes unchanged); result (either side: what a call returned, under the id of the call it answers; a result for an id the receiver never called is refused); refusal (each side: a typed refusal of one message); bye (each side, last). THE CALLER: the daemon sets the caller of every core message from the channel it came in on, never from the message: no message carries a caller, and a core message that names one is refused 'caller_forged' before the core sees it. Every csl-core/v0 op stays the core's: the host relays the bytes and decides nothing, and every call still passes the core's one dispatcher. CALL NAMES: x-call-names is ONE list, append-only, never a fixed set of message types: a later surface kind is a new name on that list and never a schema break. A call whose name the receiver does not know is refused 'call_unknown' and nothing runs; a call with a reserved name is refused 'call_reserved' with the words 'reserved; not available in this release' and nothing runs; at the daemon that refusal comes before any other check of the name. MESSAGE TYPES: a message whose type the receiver does not know is answered with a typed refusal ('message_unknown') and the channel stays up; the message names in x-reserved.message_types are reserved: named here, refused 'message_reserved' if sent in this release, never built here. x-refusal-codes lists each code this channel answers with. RUN REQUEST (x-run-request): run.request is the one call a plugin's host sends that the daemon answers. It is offered only to a plugin whose granted permissions include 'schedule' (else 'call_not_offered'); its arguments are exactly the seven of x-run-request.args, each in its form, or the call is refused 'call_args_invalid' before anything starts; no argument names a plugin: the caller is the plugin the channel was opened for. The daemon starts the run through the one admission path of the control API's run.start, with a start key it derives from the plugin, the record, its revision and the occurrence (never one the plugin gives), so the same plugin, record, revision and occurrence start at most one run for one tenant; the same occurrence for another tenant is another run, and a new occurrence starts a new one. The result's value is run.start's answer; the run's record is the one run.start writes plus one field, 'origin' (x-run-request.origin), which run.status and run.list show and which a control client's run.start cannot set.

x-call-names.name: registry
x-call-names.about: The plugin's panels for the page, as registry() returns them today.

x-call-names.name: operator
x-call-names.about: One o7.operator.v0 read command; the daemon keeps its own deadline on the answer.

x-call-names.name: surfaces
x-call-names.about: The surfaces a plugin offers (provisional: no host calls it on master).

x-call-names.name: surface
x-call-names.about: One surface by kind and name (provisional: no host calls it on master).

x-call-names.name: run.request
x-call-names.about: A plugin's host asks the daemon for a run from one of the plugin's records (x-run-request); the daemon answers with run.start's answer.

x-call-names.name: memory.put
x-call-names.about: Keep one item of the plugin's saved data: if_revision is the revision last read, or null to create only; answers the new revision (x-memory).

x-call-names.name: memory.get
x-call-names.about: Read one item of the plugin's own saved data: its value_b64, revision and written_at (x-memory).

x-call-names.name: memory.list
x-call-names.about: The keys of the plugin's own saved data in order, one page that fits one frame, with more and the after to go on from (x-memory).

x-call-names.name: memory.delete
x-call-names.about: Delete one item of the plugin's own saved data; null if_revision deletes any revision (x-memory).

x-memory.about: A plugin's saved data, kept by the daemon apart for each plugin and each install identity (the signer key id, or for an unsigned plugin its install record's origin mark). The four memory.* names are sent by a plugin's host and answered by the daemon, offered only when the person listed the plugin in the settings row plugin_memory.plugins (read when Recursion starts) AND the plugin holds the permission 'memory' at this call; else 'call_not_offered', whose detail says which grant is missing. No argument names a plugin, an install or a namespace. Every answer is a result whose value is {ok: true, ...} or {ok: false, code, what, why, next, changed}, and fits one frame: the largest value is derived from the frame limit, never a second number.
x-memory.key: 1 to 256 bytes of UTF-8 with no control character; never a file name. A list's prefix may be empty.
x-memory.value_b64: The item's bytes as standard base64 with padding.
x-memory.if_revision: null, or the revision last read (a whole number from 1).

x-run-request.about: The arguments of run.request and the origin the daemon writes into the run's record. record_kinds is append-only: a later record kind is a new name at its end. Every argument is required and none other is taken.

record_id.description: The record's id in the plugin's own store.

occurrence.description: The time the run is for: an RFC 3339 UTC time ending in Z, in whole seconds, a real instant.

tenant.description: As run.start takes it: a non-empty string.

engine.description: As run.start takes it: a non-empty string.

prompt.description: As run.start takes it: a non-empty string of strict UTF-8.

origin.about: Written by the daemon into the run's record, never taken from a message or from a control client's params: kind trigger, the plugin the channel was opened for, and the record_kind, record_id, revision and occurrence of the call.

x-reserved.about: Names reserved for later work. Each is answered as reserved, with the words 'reserved; not available in this release', and nothing is built for it here: no handler, no permission that grants anything, no record writer. These lists are append-only. Reserved is not frozen: a reserved name may be corrected until the first build that answers it. When it is built, each reserved call name here is sent by a plugin's host to the daemon (the plugin asks the core: the computer names for a computer or browser session, net.request and net.connect for the network; run.request, which asks for a run, is built and has left this list) and answered by result or refusal; that is why call and result travel both ways.

call_names.name: computer.open
call_names.about: Opens a computer or browser session for a plugin.

call_names.name: computer.act
call_names.about: One action in an open computer or browser session.

call_names.name: computer.observe
call_names.about: What an open computer or browser session shows now.

call_names.name: computer.close
call_names.about: Ends a computer or browser session.

call_names.name: net.request
call_names.about: The core makes an HTTPS request to a granted destination and returns the answer.

call_names.name: net.connect
call_names.about: The core connects to a granted destination and hands the connected socket to the host.

message_types.name: event
message_types.about: An event delivered to a host that subscribed to it.

message_types.name: guard
message_types.about: An ask-or-deny round trip with a deadline.

message_types.name: surface.update
message_types.about: A surface update the host starts.

run_origin.name: trigger
run_origin.about: A run started by a scheduled task or another trigger.

run_origin.name: agent
run_origin.about: A run started by a persistent agent.

run_origin.name: packet
run_origin.about: A run started by a work packet from another node.

x-reserved.run_origin_about: Where a run came from. No message on this channel carries a run's origin yet, so no field is made for it: the three values are reserved here by name, and their refusal is placed when a field carries them. The run record's 'origin' (x-run-request.origin) is written by the daemon when it answers run.request, never taken from a message; it carries kind 'trigger' only, and 'agent' and 'packet' are written nowhere yet.

x-inventory.about: Every function the daemon calls on a plugin, and the one message that carries it. registry, operator and bind_core are what daemon/plugins.py calls today; surfaces and surface are the provisional ones of the themes plugin.

x-refusal-codes.message_invalid: The message is not one object of a known type with exactly its fields and their forms, or it is a result for an id the receiver never called.
x-refusal-codes.message_unknown: The receiver does not know the message type; the channel stays up.
x-refusal-codes.message_reserved: The message type is reserved; not available in this release. The channel stays up.
x-refusal-codes.message_wrong_side: The message type is known but is never sent by this side of the channel.
x-refusal-codes.caller_forged: A core message named a caller; the caller is set from the channel, so nothing reached the core.
x-refusal-codes.call_unknown: The receiver does not know the call name; nothing ran.
x-refusal-codes.call_reserved: The call name is reserved; not available in this release. Nothing ran.
x-refusal-codes.call_args_invalid: The call's arguments are not exactly the ones listed for its name; nothing ran.
x-refusal-codes.call_not_offered: The receiver does not offer this call (a plugin that has no function for it, or at the daemon a call the plugin is not granted); nothing ran.
x-refusal-codes.call_failed: The plugin's function raised; the detail names the exception's type only.
x-refusal-codes.load_too_large: The daemon's side: a package does not fit one load frame, so no load is sent; never a frame error.

id.description: A message id, chosen by the side that sends the request and echoed by the answer.

bytes.description: Bytes as standard base64 with padding.

call_name.description: A name on the one append-only list x-call-names, or a reserved one, or one this receiver does not know: lower-case dotted words.

hello.description: The first message each side sends, naming the channel's version.

load.description: Daemon to host: one plugin to load, as bytes the daemon has already verified; it names the plugin the channel was opened for, and one load frame may be as large as the daemon's largest package needs. load may arrive after hello at any time, even though the daemon sends it only at start in this release.

files.description: Every verified file of the package: its path inside the package and its bytes.

call.description: Either side: one call by NAME (the daemon calls a plugin's function; a plugin's host calls a broker handle). Which arguments a name takes is listed for it in x-call-names; the receiver refuses any other set.

args.description: The call's arguments by name; each value is the argument's own data.

additionalProperties.description: One argument's value, as the call's name defines it.

core.description: One csl-core/v0 request (host to daemon) or answer (daemon to host), its bytes unchanged. It carries no caller: the daemon sets the caller from the channel.

result.description: Either side: what one call returned, under the call's id. A result for an id the receiver never called is refused.

value.description: The plugin's own return value, as plain JSON.

refusal.description: Either side: a typed refusal of one message. id is the refused message's id, or null when it had none that could be read.

bye.description: Either side, last: the channel ends.
